does: Stirs ground spices into the hot fat already in the pan, with the meat or onions, for a short moment before the liquid goes in, which deepens their flavour and takes away their raw, dusty taste.
how: Make sure there is a little fat in the pan, and lower the heat to medium.
Scatter in the ground spices and stir so that they coat everything.
Fry for a moment, stirring, until they smell toasty and darken a shade.
Add the liquid before they can scorch.

cues.text: A warm, toasty scent that fills the kitchen.
The spices darken a shade and coat the meat or onions evenly.

mistakes.mistake: Frying them over a high heat or for too long, so that they scorch and turn bitter.
mistakes.fix: Lower the heat first and add the liquid as soon as they smell toasty.

mistakes.mistake: Adding them with the liquid, so that they taste raw and dusty.
mistakes.fix: Give them their moment in the fat first.

variant_of.differs: Ground spices are stirred into the fat already in the pan with the meat or onions at a moderate heat, rather than whole seeds sizzled in a separate spoonful of very hot fat and poured over.
